housingAlert: The most common scam: a 'landlord' asks for the deposit by transfer before any viewing, then disappears. Never pay before seeing the room and signing.
Check the address exists and that the person is the owner or an authorised agency. Ask for ID and a written contract.
Prices well below the area average are a red flag.
Use your university's housing service and the student community to cross-check offers.

tasks.title: Health insurance (EHIC)
tasks.description: EU citizens use the European Health Insurance Card for medically necessary care during a temporary stay. It is free and requested from your own health insurer before leaving. It does not cover private care, rescue or repatriation.
steps: Request the EHIC before you travel
Check it covers your whole stay
tasks.officialSourceName: Your Europe – Health cover for temporary stays

tasks.title: Accommodation (scam check)
tasks.description: Finding a room is the most stressful step reported by students in Milan, and scams are frequent. Follow the scam checklist before paying any deposit. You need the address for the Anagrafe registration.

tasks.title: Italian tax code
tasks.description: Information online is often contradictory. Official rule: for a first codice fiscale you book an in-person appointment at an Agenzia delle Entrate office (EU and non-EU citizens). Non-EU citizens can also apply at a Sportello Unico per l'immigrazione or a Questura.
documentsNeeded: Non-EU: passport with visa or residence permit
steps: Book an appointment at an Agenzia delle Entrate office
Bring your ID and the request form

tasks.title: Municipal registration
tasks.description: Many students don't know this is required. EU citizens staying more than 3 months register with the Anagrafe of their municipality (not during the first 3 months). Documents: proof of enrolment, comprehensive health insurance and a declaration of sufficient resources.
steps: Find the Comune di Milano registration service
